sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: team hierarchy queries — find direct reports; employment_status: filtering active/inactive/terminated employees; deleted_at: soft-delete filtering

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, leave_type, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: list leave requests for a specific employee; status: filter by status (SUBMITTED, APPROVED, etc.); leave_policy_id: filter by policy; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: manager approval history queries; employee_id + status: combined filter for employee dashboard

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: lookup policy by leave type (annual, sick, emergency); is_active: filter active policies only

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: lookup balances for a specific employee; policy_id: filter balances by policy; fiscal_year: filter by fiscal year; employee_id + policy_id + fiscal_year: unique constraint — one balance row per employee per policy per fiscal year

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type + entity_id: audit trail lookup for a specific entity; performed_by: audit trail by actor; performed_at: time-range audit queries; action: filter by action type (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT)

table notifications | fields: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at | pk: id | fks: recipient_id -> employees.id | indexes: recipient_id: list notifications for a specific user; status: filter by PENDING/SENT/READ/ARCHIVED; related_entity_type + related_entity_id: find notifications related to a specific entity (e.g. a leave request); created_at: chronological ordering

data_notes: Persistence slice defined with 6 conceptual tables (employees, leave_requests, leave_policies, leave_balances, audit_logs, notifications), 5 repository interfaces with concrete Pg* implementations backed by PostgreSQL via pg Pool, and 1 open question on balance computation strategy (derived vs materialized vs hybrid). All tables reference the existing domain model from docs/DOMAIN.md. Audit table (audit_logs) satisfies GP-002. All DB access goes through repository interfaces per GP-001.

open_questions.question: How are leave_balances.used_days and remaining_days computed — are they derived live from approved leave_requests (sum of day counts) or are they materialized and updated transactionally on each approval/rejection?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether the balance repository needs a transactional update path tied to leave request status changes, or whether balances are computed via aggregate queries. Affects data consistency guarantees and the design of the approval workflow.
candidate_options: Derived live: used_days = SUM(day count) from approved leave_requests for the employee/policy/fiscal_year. remaining_days = total_entitlement - used_days. No materialized writes to leave_balances.used_days.
Materialized transactional: on each APPROVE/REJECT/CANCEL of a leave_request, atomically update leave_balances.used_days and remaining_days within the same transaction.
Hybrid: materialized as a cache, with a periodic reconciliation job that recalculates from leave_requests.
